newsitem.title: USA: Dillon, Read to be acquired by Swiss Bank.
newsitem.headline: Dillon, Read to be acquired by Swiss Bank.

text.p: Dillon, Read & Co Inc said Thursday it agreed to be acquired by Swiss Bank Corp for about $600 million and merged with SBC Warburg, the bank's investment banking and capital markets division.

Dillon Read is owned and controlled by its management, who control 75 percent of the equity in the firm. ING Barings has a 25 percent economic interest and will receive the same consideration upon closing as management shareholders.
Upon completion of the acquisition, the combined company will be known as SBC Warburg Dillon Read. The transaction is dependent upon the approval of the U.S. Federal Reserve.

Early Thursday, ING Group said it had writhdraw from talks on the purchase of the remaining 75 percent of Dillon Read, explaining the two parties could not reach an agreement on an organizational structure under which Dillon Read would become integrated with ING's corporate and investment banking business.
ING said its management expects Dillon Read's partners to exercise their option to repurchase ING's 25 percent stake in the firm.

The combination of Dillon Read and SBC Warburg "is an excellent fit for both firms, as it will enhance significantly the capabilities and resources we are able to offer our clients and the career opportunities available to our staff," said Dillon Read chief exeuctive Franklin Hobbs.

"We especially look forward to offering our clients access to SBC Warburg's enormous range of products and services, which span every area of specialized advisory service, capital markets expertise, and risk management products."

With acquisition, Dillon Read said, SBC Warburg will gain a substantial presence in the United States in corporate finance, mergers and acquisitions and U.S. equity and debt underwriting. Dillon Read will get a new platform from which to enhance its equity and high-yield areas.

SBC Warburg had revenues of $3.5 billion in 1996 and profit before taxes of $759 million, representing 44 percent of the Swiss Bank's profit before taxes. SBC Warburg has 9,000 employees, 2,000 of whom are located in the United States.

John Birkelund, chairman of Dillon Read, said, "This acquisition not only responds to the globalization and consolidation taking place in the investment banking industry but also creates a world of opportunity for our clients and employees."

Founded in 1832, Dillon Read has 730 employees spread among offices in New York, Boston, San Francisco, Dallas, London, Paris and Tokyo. In 1996, it was among the leading merger and acquisition advisors having completed 50 deals with an aggregate value of $45 billion. The company is also active in the high yield, equity and private placement markets, having completed transactions valued at over $8 billion in these markets in 1996.
After the acquisition, Hobbs will serve as head of corporate finance worldwide of SBC Warburg Dillon Read and will be based in London.
Francois de Saint Phalle, Dillon Read vice chairman and chief operating officer, has been named its deputy head of equity capital markets worldwide and co-head of U.S. equities.
Birkelund will continue to occupy a leadership role in the combined organization.
